rules.title: Housing discrimination and lawful source-of-income protections
rules.requirement: A landlord may not discriminate in renting housing or in rental terms based on protected characteristics or a tenant’s lawful source of income, including Section 8 voucher income. Landlords also may not use discriminatory advertising, falsely deny availability, charge extra for a service or guide dog, or refuse reasonable disability-related modifications at the tenant’s expense.

coverage.other_unresolvable: Exceptions include renting a room in an owner-occupied one-family dwelling, religious-organization preferences for persons of the same religion, and the familial-status prohibition not applying to housing for older persons as defined in the LAD.
coverage.summary: Applies to the sale or rental of all property, including residential property, except certain owner-occupied small dwellings and specified religious-organization and housing-for-older-persons situations.

rules.exemptions: The document lists exceptions for rental of a single apartment or flat in an owner-occupied two-family dwelling; rental of rooms by the owner or occupant of an owner-occupied one-family dwelling; religious-organization preferences for persons of the same religion; and housing for older persons for the familial-status prohibition.
rules.quoted_span:
The LAD also prohibits housing discrimination  based
on the source of lawful income or source of lawful rent
or mortgage payment a tenant or purchaser uses. This
means, for example, that a landlord cannot deny the
lawful recipient of a Section 8 HUD voucher the right to
rent an apartment based solely on that source of lawful
income.
